meta.title: Directive (EU) 2016/1919 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 October 2016 on legal aid for suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and for requested persons in European arrest warrant proceedings

items.heading: Article 1

items.text: 1. This Directive lays down common minimum rules concerning the right to legal aid for:
items.comment: In French legal system, the main legislation concerning legal aid is Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid and Decree No. 91-1266 of 19 December 1991 implementing Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

items.text: (a)suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings; and

nationalActs.title: Loi n° 91-647 du 10 juillet 1991 relative à l'aide juridique
nationalActs.titleEn: Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

provisions.textEn: Legal aid is granted in ex gratia or contentious proceedings, as a claimant or defendant in front of any jurisdiction, as well as during the procedure for hearing minors provided for by article 388-1 of the Civil Code and during the procedure for appearing in court upon prior recognition of guilt (réconnaissance péalable de culpabilité) provided for by articles 495-7 et seq. of the Code of Criminal Procedure. (…)

items.comment: Legal aid in criminal proceedings was amended by law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991: legal aid is no longer limited to civil parties and persons civilly liable but is now extended to all parties before all criminal jurisdictions

items.text: (b)persons who are the subject of European arrest warrant proceedings pursuant to Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA (requested persons).

nationalActs.title: Code de procédure pénale
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of criminal procedure

provisions.textEn: (...) After verifying the identity of the person concerned, the public prosecutor shall inform him, in a language he understands, of the existence and content of the European arrest warrant against him. He shall also inform him that he may be assisted by a lawyer of his choice or, failing that, by a lawyer appointed by the President of the Bar Association, informed without delay and by any means. He shall likewise inform her that she may speak immediately with the lawyer designated.

items.comment: No specific article providing for legal aid for persons whose surrender is requested. The requested person has the right to the assistance of a lawyer of his or her choice or, in failing that, one assigned by the court, as provided for in article 695-27 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. If the conditions for receiving legal aid are satisfied legal aid is granted.

items.text: 2. This Directive complements Directives 2013/48/EU and (EU) 2016/800. Nothing in this Directive shall be interpreted as limiting the rights provided for in those Directives.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. This Directive applies to suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings who have a right of access to a lawyer pursuant to Directive 2013/48/EU and who are:

items.text: (a)deprived of liberty;

nationalActs.title: Loi n° 91-647 du 10 juillet 1991 relative à l'aide juridique
nationalActs.titleEn: Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

provisions.textEn: A person who has benefited from the intervention of a court-appointed lawyer under the conditions laid down in Article 63-3-1 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and who is not eligible for legal aid is required to reimburse the Treasury for the sums incurred by the State. The recovery of sums due to the State takes place as in the case of claims outside the tax and estate fields.

items.comment: Since the reform of police custody (law of 14 April 2011), from the beginning of police custody, the person can ask to be assisted by a lawyer. If the person is unable to choose a lawyer or if the lawyer chosen cannot be contacted, he or she may request that one be appointed by the President of the Bar Association. The appointed lawyer may assist the person placed in police custody during an initial interview limited to 30 minutes, but also during hearings and confrontations (art. 63-3-1). If the conditions for receiving legal aid are met, legal aid is granted.

items.text: (b)required to be assisted by a lawyer in accordance with Union or national law; or
items.comment: There is no specific text law of 10 july 1991 providing for legal aid to be granted to suspect or accused person who are required to be assisted by a lawyer in accordance with Union or national law but the law generally provides that when the conditions for obtaining legal aid are satisfied, the charges which would be incurred by the beneficiary of legal aid if he did not have this aid are borne by the State (art. 24 law 1991).

items.text: (c)required or permitted to attend an investigative or evidence-gathering act, including as a minimum the following:

nationalActs.title: Loi n° 91-647 du 10 juillet 1991 relative à l'aide juridique
nationalActs.titleEn: Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

provisions.textEn: The lawyer assisting, during the hearing, confrontation or investigation measures mentioned in articles 61-1 to 61-3 of the code of criminal procedure, in article L. 39 of the tax procedure code or in article 67 F of the customs code, the suspected person who satisfies the conditions to benefit from legal aid has the right to remuneration

items.comment: The person questioned in police or gendarmerie offices other than police custody must be informed of the option available to him or her between the free choice of counsel and the designation by the President of the Bar of his or her own motion. The Act of 27 May 2014 amended article 64 of the Legal Aid Act, which provides for the granting of legal aid if the lawyer is assisted in this situation. The police or gendarmerie shall inform the person that, unless he or she satisfies the conditions for the granting of legal aid, the costs of a lawyer shall be charged to him or her if he or she applies for the designation of a public-appointed lawyer.

items.text: (i)identity parades;
(ii)confrontations;
(iii)reconstructions of the scene of a crime.
2. This Directive also applies, upon arrest in the executing Member State, to requested persons who have a right of access to a lawyer pursuant to Directive 2013/48/EU.
items.comment: No specific article providing for legal aid for persons whose surrender is requested. The requested person has the right to the assistance of a lawyer of his or her choice or, in failing that, one assigned by the court, as provided for in article 695-27 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. If the conditions for receiving legal aid are satisfied, legal aid is granted.

items.text: 3. This Directive also applies, under the same conditions as provided for in paragraph 1, to persons who were not initially suspects or accused persons but become suspects or accused persons in the course of questioning by the police or by another law enforcement authority.

nationalActs.titleEn: Code of criminal procedure

provisions.textEn:
5° If the offence for which she is being heard is punishable by a prison sentence, she has the right to be assisted during her hearing or confrontation, in accordance with the procedures provided for in Articles 63-4-3 and 63-4-4-4, by a lawyer chosen by her or, at her request, appointed ex officio by the President of the Bar Association ; she is informed that the costs will be borne by her unless she meets the conditions for access to legal aid, which are reminded to her by any means; she may expressly agree to continue the hearing without the presence of her lawyer ;

Art. 63-1 reference to Art. 63-3-1 From the beginning of police custody, the person may request to be assisted by a lawyer. If he is unable to appoint one or if the lawyer chosen cannot be contacted, he may request that the President of the Bar appoint one for him ex officio.

items.comment:
During the hearing of a person heard freely, where it appears that there are plausible grounds for suspecting that he has committed or attempted to commit an offence, he may either be taken into custody or be kept under the regime of free hearing (art. 62 c.p.p.). Even if she is not taken into police custody she shall have the right to the assistance of a lawyer.

However, this assistance is possible only if the offence about which the suspect is being heard is an offence punishable by imprisonment. In this case, as provided for in Article 61-1 5°, the assistance will be paid as legal aid if the person satisfies the conditions required by law.

Article 62 of the Code of Criminal Procedure provides that persons against whom there is no plausible reason to suspect that they have committed or attempted to commit an offence shall be heard by investigators without being subjected to a coercive measure.

However, if justified by the needs of the investigation, such persons may be held under restraint for the time strictly necessary for their hearing, which may not exceed four hours.

If, during the hearing of a person heard freely in accordance with the first paragraph of this Article, it appears that there are plausible grounds for suspecting that he or she has committed or attempted to commit an offence, that person must be heard in accordance with Article 61-1 and the information provided for in 1° to 6° of the same Article shall then be notified to him or her without delay, unless his or her placement in police custody is necessary in accordance with Article 62-2.

If, during the hearing of a person detained pursuant to the second paragraph of this Article, it appears that there are plausible grounds for suspecting that he or she has committed or attempted to commit a crime or an offence punishable by a prison penalty, she may only be kept under police custody. He shall then be notified of his detention in police custody under the conditions laid down in Article 63-1.

items.text: 4. Without prejudice to the right to a fair trial, in respect of minor offences:

(a)where the law of a Member State provides for the imposition of a sanction by an authority other than a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters, and the imposition of such a sanction may be appealed or referred to such a court; or
(b)where deprivation of liberty cannot be imposed as a sanction;
this Directive applies only to the proceedings before a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters.
In any event, this Directive applies when a decision on detention is taken, and during detention, at any stage of the proceedings until the conclusion of the proceedings.
For the purposes of this Directive, ‘legal aid’ means funding by a Member State of the assistance of a lawyer, enabling the exercise of the right of access to a lawyer.
items.heading: Article 3

nationalActs.title: Loi n° 91-647 du 10 juillet 1991 relative à l'aide juridique
nationalActs.titleEn: Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

provisions.textEn:
Natural persons with insufficient resources to assert their rights in legal proceedings may receive legal aid. This aid is total or partial.

Exceptionally, legal aid may be granted to non-profit legal entities having their registered office in France and not having sufficient resources. (…)

nationalActs.title: Loi n° 91-647 du 10 juillet 1991 relative à l'aide juridique
nationalActs.titleEn: Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

provisions.textEn:
Legal aid covers all legal costs relating to the proceedings, procedures or acts for which it has been granted, with the exception of pleading rights.

The beneficiary of the aid is exempted from the payment, advance or deposit of such costs.

The costs of investigative measures are paid in advance by the State.

items.comment:
The 1991 law does not provide a proper definition of legal aid. Legal aid covers all charges relating to the proceedings, procedures or acts for which it has been granted, including the charges relating to investigative measures. It is a financial aid which enables persons without resources or on a limited income to benefit from the payment by the State of all or part of the lawyer's fees and the costs of the proceedings.

Legal aid should not be confused with aid for access to the right, which includes aid for consultation and assistance during non-judicial proceedings.

items.heading: Article 4

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons who lack sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a lawyer have the right to legal aid when the interests of justice so require.

items.text: 2. Member States may apply a means test, a merits test, or both to determine whether legal aid is to be granted in accordance with paragraph 1.

nationalActs.title: Loi n° 91-647 du 10 juillet 1991 relative à l'aide juridique
nationalActs.titleEn: Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

provisions.textEn:
Natural persons with insufficient resources to assert their rights in legal proceedings may receive legal aid. This aid is total or partial.

Exceptionally, legal aid may be granted to non-profit legal entities having their registered office in France and not having sufficient resources.

nationalActs.title: Loi n° 91-647 du 10 juillet 1991 relative à l'aide juridique
nationalActs.titleEn: Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

provisions.textEn:
Legal aid shall be granted to a person whose action does not appear to be manifestly inadmissible, unfounded or abusive due in particular to the number of requests, their repeated or systematic nature.This condition shall not apply to the defendant in the action, the person civilly liable, the witness, the suspect, the accused person, the condemned person and the person subject to the procedure of comparution sur reconnaissance préalable de culpabilité.

Furthermore, in cassation proceedings, legal aid is denied to the applicant if no serious grounds for cassation can be raised.

items.comment:
In order to obtain legal aid, a means test and a merit test must be satisfied.

Firstly, aid is granted only if the person cannot cover the legal fees.

The aid may be total or partial according to a means test, the level of which can be modified at the beginning of each year.


Decree No. 91-1266 of 19 December 1991 implementing Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 on legal aid details the conditions of resources (1st section of the decree) and the ceiling of resources (Article 98).


Secondly, aid may be granted only to persons whose action does not appear to be manifestly inadmissible, unfounded or abusive due in particular to the number of requests, their repeated or systematic nature.However, this last condition is not required of the defendant, the person civilly liable, the witness, the suspect, the accused person, the condemned person and the person subject to the procedure of comparution sur reconnaissance préalable de culpabilité.

items.text: 3. Where a Member State applies a means test, it shall take into account all relevant and objective factors, such as the income, capital and family situation of the person concerned, as well as the costs of the assistance of a lawyer and the standard of living in that Member State, in order to determine whether, in accordance with the applicable criteria in that Member State, a suspect or an accused person lacks sufficient resources to pay for the assistance of a lawyer.

nationalActs.title: Loi n° 91-647 du 10 juillet 1991 relative à l'aide juridique
nationalActs.titleEn: Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

provisions.textEn:
I.- The annual ceilings of eligibility of natural people to legal aid are set by decree in the Council of State. 

II-The insufficient nature of the resources of natural persons is assessed taking into account :

1° The reference tax income or, failing this, the taxable income, the calculation methods of which are defined by decree;

2° the capital value of movable or immovable assets, even if they do not generate income; 

3° The composition of the tax household.

III- Assets which could not be sold or pledged without causing serious trouble for the interested parties are not taken into account in the calculation of the amount of resources to which the eligibility ceilings apply.

nationalActs.title: Loi n° 91-647 du 10 juillet 1991 relative à l'aide juridique
nationalActs.titleEn: Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

provisions.textEn:
The assessment of resources is personalised in the following cases:

1° The procedure opposes persons within the same tax household or there is a divergence of interest between them, having regard to the object of the conflict;

2° The procedure concerns a major or minor person attached to the tax household of his/her parents or legal representatives, who show a lack of interest towards him/her.

items.comment:
All resources are considered, including those of the spouse and persons usually living at home (unless the action is brought against the applicant for aid).

External elements of lifestyle, movable or immovable property even if they do not produce any income are also taken into account but excluding those which could not be sold or pledged without 'causing serious trouble to the person concerned'.

items.text: 4. Where a Member State applies a merits test, it shall take into account the seriousness of the criminal offence, the complexity of the case and the severity of the sanction at stake, in order to determine whether the interests of justice require legal aid to be granted. In any event, the merits test shall be deemed to have been met in the following situations:
items.comment: In criminal proceedings, the "means test" provided for by Directive 2016/1919, which is set out in Article 7 of the Law of 10 July 1991, according to which the action "does not appear to be manifestly inadmissible or unfounded" (Article 7 of the Law), is not applicable to the defendant to the action, the civilly liable person, the witness, the suspect, the accused or condemned person and the defendant in the procedure of comparution sur reconnaissance préalable de culpabilité (the person subject to the procedure of prior recognition of guilt).

items.text: (a)where a suspect or an accused person is brought before a competent court or judge in order to decide on detention at any stage of the proceedings within the scope of this Directive; and
items.comment: See above

items.text: (b)during detention.
items.comment: See above

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that legal aid is granted without undue delay, and at the latest before questioning by the police, by another law enforcement authority or by a judicial authority, or before the investigative or evidence-gathering acts referred to in point (c) of Article 2(1) are carried out.
6. Legal aid shall be granted only for the purposes of the criminal proceedings in which the person concerned is suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Legal aid in European arrest warrant proceedings

items.text: 1. The executing Member State shall ensure that requested persons have a right to legal aid upon arrest pursuant to a European arrest warrant until they are surrendered, or until the decision not to surrender them becomes final.

nationalActs.title: Code de procédure pénale
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of criminal procedure

provisions.textEn:
Any person apprehended in execution of a European arrest warrant shall be taken within 48 hours before the Public Prosecutor territorially competent. During that period, Articles 63(1) to 63(7) are applicable.

After verifying the identity of the person concerned, the Public Prosecutor shall inform him or her, in a language which he or she understands, of the existence and content of the European arrest warrant against him or her. He shall also inform him that he may be assisted by a lawyer of his choice or, failing that, by a lawyer appointed by the President of the Bar Association, informed without delay and by any means. He shall likewise inform her that she may speak immediately with the lawyer appointed.

The Public Prosecutor shall also inform the person that he or she may request to be assisted in the issuing Member State by a lawyer of his or her own choice or by a lawyer appointed by the Bar Association; if the person so requests, the request shall be forwarded forthwith to the competent judicial authority in the issuing Member State.

﻿Mention of this information must be made in the report, otherwise the procedure will be invalidated.

The lawyer appointed in accordance with the second subparagraph may consult the file immediately and communicate with the requested person without restriction.

items.comment: No specific article providing for legal aid for persons whose surrender is requested. The requested person has the right to the assistance of a lawyer of his or her choice or, in failing that, one assigned by the court, as provided for in article 695-27 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. If the conditions for receiving legal aid are satisfied, legal aid is granted.

items.text: 2. The issuing Member State shall ensure that requested persons who are the subject of European arrest warrant proceedings for the purpose of conducting a criminal prosecution and who exercise their right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State to assist the lawyer in the executing Member State in accordance with Article 10(4) and (5) of Directive 2013/48/EU have the right to legal aid in the issuing Member State for the purpose of such proceedings in the executing Member State, in so far as legal aid is necessary to ensure effective access to justice.

nationalActs.title: Code de procédure pénale
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of criminal procedure

provisions.comment: This article has been created by law n°2016-731 of 3 June 2016 - art. 63
provisions.textEn: If the Public Prosecutor is informed by the judicial authority of the executing Member State of a request from the arrested person for the appointment of a lawyer in the national territory, the Prosecutor must provide that person with the relevant information enabling him to choose a lawyer or, at the request of the person, have a lawyer appointed by the President of the Bar.

items.comment: No specific article providing for legal aid for persons who are the subject of European arrest warrant proceedings for the purpose of conducting a criminal prosecution and who exercise their right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing Member State to assist the lawyer in the executing Member State in accordance with Article 10(4) and (5) of Directive 2013/48/EU. The requested person has the right to the assistance of a lawyer of his or her choice or, in failing that, one assigned by the court, to assist the lawyer in the executing Member State, as provided for in article 695-17-1 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. If the conditions for receiving legal aid are satisfied, legal aid is granted.

items.text: 3. The right to legal aid referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 may be subject to a means test in accordance with Article 4(3), which shall apply mutatis mutandis.
items.comment: The resource condition (art. 2 law 1991) is a general condition applicable to all procedures, except for some hypotheses where resources are not considered (see below).

items.heading: Article 6
items.subHeading: Decisions regarding the granting of legal aid

items.text: 1. Decisions on whether or not to grant legal aid and on the assignment of lawyers shall be made, without undue delay, by a competent authority. Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that the competent authority takes its decisions diligently, respecting the rights of the defence.

nationalActs.title: Loi n° 91-647 du 10 juillet 1991 relative à l'aide juridique
nationalActs.titleEn: Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

provisions.textEn: Admission to legal aid is pronounced by a legal aid office.

items.comment:
The authority specifically competent to decide on the application for legal aid is the legal aid office.

Articles 12-17 of the law regulate the organisation of legal aid offices.

items.text: 2. Member States shall take necessary measures to ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons are informed in writing if their request for legal aid is refused in full or in part.

nationalActs.title: Décret n°91-1266 du 19 décembre 1991 portant application de la loi n° 91-647 du 10 juillet 1991 relative à l'aide juridique
nationalActs.titleEn: Decree No. 91-1266 of 19 December 1991 implementing Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

provisions.textEn:
A copy of the decision of the office, the section of the office or their president is notified to the applicant by the secretary of the office or the section of the office by simple letter in the case of admission to full legal aid, and by means of any device enabling the date of receipt to be certified in other cases.

The notification of the decision refusing legal aid, granting it only partially or withdrawing the benefit of legal aid specifies how the applicant may appeal against the decision.

(…)

items.heading: Article 7
items.subHeading: Quality of legal aid services and training

items.text: 1. Member States shall take necessary measures, including with regard to funding, to ensure that:
(a)there is an effective legal aid system that is of an adequate quality; and
(b)legal aid services are of a quality adequate to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, with due respect for the independence of the legal profession.
2. Member States shall ensure that adequate training is provided to staff involved in the decision-making on legal aid in criminal proceedings and in European arrest warrant proceedings.

3. With due respect for the independence of the legal profession and for the role of those responsible for the training of lawyers, Member States shall take appropriate measures to promote the provision of adequate training to lawyers providing legal aid services.

4. Member States shall take the necessary measures to ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons have the right, upon their request, to have the lawyer providing legal aid services assigned to them replaced, where the specific circumstances so justify.

nationalActs.title: Décret n°91-1266 du 19 décembre 1991 portant application de la loi n° 91-647 du 10 juillet 1991 relative à l'aide juridique
nationalActs.titleEn: Decree No. 91-1266 of 19 December 1991 implementing Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

provisions.textEn:
Where a lawyer appointed or chosen under legal aid is, during the proceedings, replaced by another lawyer for the same title due to a legitimate reason, only one contribution from the State is due. This contribution is paid to the second lawyer, who must share with the first lawyer in a proportion which, in the absence of agreement, is fixed by the President of the Bar.

If the lawyers are not members of the same Bar, the decision is taken jointly by the Presidents of the Bars concerned.

The same rules are applicable when the replacement takes place during transactional talks.

items.comment:
If the lawyer has been designated by legal aid, it is possible to change the lawyer if serious reasons are given. A registered letter with return receipt must be sent to the President of the Bar of the said lawyer, stating the precise reasons for the request for change.

When a lawyer appointed or chosen under the legal aid scheme is replaced by another during the course of the proceedings, he is not totally deprived of his right to remuneration: the legal aid allowance is given to the second lawyer, but he must share it with the first (Decree 91-1266 of 19 December 1991).

items.text: Member States shall ensure that suspects, accused persons and requested persons have an effective remedy under national law in the event of a breach of their rights under this Directive.
items.heading: Article 8

nationalActs.title: Loi n° 91-647 du 10 juillet 1991 relative à l'aide juridique
nationalActs.titleEn: Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

provisions.textEn: Appeals against the decisions of the legal aid office may be made by the person concerned when the benefit of legal aid has been refused, has been granted only partially or has been withdrawn.

nationalActs.title: Décret n°91-1266 du 19 décembre 1991 portant application de la loi n° 91-647 du 10 juillet 1991 relative à l'aide juridique
nationalActs.titleEn: Decree No. 91-1266 of 19 December 1991 implementing Law No. 91-647 of 10 July 1991 concerning legal aid

provisions.comment: Articles 56 to 60 of the decree provide detailed rules for appeals against the decisions of the offices.
provisions.textEn: A copy of the decision of the Bureau, Bureau Section or their President shall be notified to the person concerned by the Secretary of the Bureau or Bureau Section by ordinary letter in the case of admission to full legal aid, and by any means of proof of the date of receipt in other cases. The notification of the decision refusing legal aid, granting it only partially or withdrawing the benefit of this aid indicates the modalities according to which the person concerned may appeal against this decision. (…)

items.text: Member States shall ensure that the particular needs of vulnerable suspects, accused persons and requested persons are taken into account in the implementation of this Directive.
items.heading: Article 9
items.comment:
The means test is applicable to all those applying for legal aid, regardless of nationality, with the exception of three categories who are entitled to legal aid without any income or assets test:

- Minors whose parents lose interest: Article 5 of the law of 10 July 1991 on legal aid allows minors whose parents lose interest to be assisted by legal aid, regardless of their parents' resources.

- Victims of crimes and deliberate attacks on their life or integrity (attempted murder, acts of barbarism, rape) (art. 9-2 of the Act);

- Exceptionally, persons whose "situation appears particularly worthy of interest regarding the object of the dispute or the expected charges of the trial" (Law of 10 July 1991, art. 6): these persons must then demonstrate that their resources, although above the thresholds for legal aid, are insufficient to ensure their defence.
